sources.claim: Quantpedia's 'Momentum Factor and Style Rotation Effect' strategy (source paper Tibbs, Eakins, DeShurko): rank six Russell equity style ETFs (small/mid/large-cap value and growth) by 12-month price momentum monthly, go long the winner and short the loser, holding one month. Reported backtest 1972-2005: annualized return 9.25%, Sharpe 0.33, volatility ~16.0%, max drawdown -52.5%. The page discloses no update or decay statement past 2005 and no long-only or recent-window figure.
sources.market_and_period: 6 Russell style ETFs, monthly, 1972-2005 (old, long-short, pre-modern-single-factor-ETF sample)
sources.applicability: Grounds the FACTOR menu's mechanism (cross-sectional momentum across style ETFs); the menu itself (MTUM/QUAL/USMV/VLUE/SIZE) and grid parameters are this batch's own choice, reusing the already-live rotation_cell engine, not copied from this source's exact parameters.
sources.limitations: Practitioner summary, not the original paper; sample ends 2005, long-short, weak standalone Sharpe (0.33); no recent-window or long-only figure disclosed.
sources.independent_replication: No independent third-party live/forward record of a long-only rotation across the modern single-factor ETF set found in this or a prior gap-search round.
